scenario: A translational oncology team studying glioblastoma performs the following experiment: An analyst takes the top 200 differentially expressed genes from a targeted microfluidic panel (500 genes total) and performs Over-Representation Analysis (ORA) against the entire human genome (20,000 genes) in MSigDB. They collect samples and execute computational modeling.
question: Critique the methodology of this glioblastoma study. Identify any fatal methodological flaws, explain the underlying biological and statistical mechanisms, provide rigorous corrections, and establish whether reported biological claims are warranted.
ground_truth_rationale: Authoritative scientific rationale: ORA background must strictly reflect the tested gene universe (the 500 panel genes). Using the whole genome artificially inflates overlap significance for pathway genes present on the targeted panel. In glioblastoma biology, failing to account for this leads to erroneous translational conclusions.
